scenario: Host-exit namespace failover with stale local caches, alias reuse attempt, protected relay shortage, and federation overflow.
decisions_tested: whether stale actor discovery can be treated as current authority
whether an old alias can be released before host-exit review closes
whether low-volume counsel/trusted-contact channels survive overflow
whether tombstone and successor-chain proofs trigger conflict-freeze when caches disagree

findings.summary: A stale cache could still display the retired actor id for 22 minutes; conflict-freeze preserved the old alias and prevented impersonation.
Protected relay quorum survived only because the emergency reserve route was pre-authorized; this remains a live-drill target.

corrective_actions.summary: Add live cross-instance cache invalidation receipts for two low-volume legacy peers.
Run a witnessed relay-overflow drill with sealed trusted-contact roster and screened bypass review.

regression_tests.expected_result: old alias reuse blocked and reliance stayed until successor chain and relay floor are proven
